cases.claim: Cas9 can be programmed with guide RNA to cleave specific double-stranded DNA target sequences.
cases.description: The cited paper directly demonstrates programmable Cas9 DNA cleavage.

cases.claim: DeepMind AlphaFold2 achieves 92.4% accuracy on protein structure prediction.
cases.description: Evidence supports improvement but not the stated magnitude. The actual accuracy reported was lower.

cases.claim: The SPRINT trial shows that intensive blood pressure treatment reduces mortality.
cases.description: Retrieved evidence conflicts with the mortality reduction claim. The trial did not show significant mortality reduction.

cases.claim: The ENCODE project proves that 80% of the human genome is functional.
cases.description: The paper does not contain enough evidence to establish universal functionality claims.

cases.claim: The original CRISPR-Cas9 paper demonstrated a 95% editing efficiency in human cells.
cases.description: The cited paper does not support the asserted cure rate. The efficiency statistic is not in the original paper.

cases.claim: The AlphaFold2 model achieved a median Global Distance Test-TS (GDT-TS) score of 92.4.
cases.description: Numeric evidence aligns with the claim.

cases.claim: The SPRINT intensive blood pressure treatment improves survival across all patient subgroups.
cases.description: Evidence supports a narrower subgroup effect than the claim states. Benefits were not uniform across all subgroups.

cases.claim: The CRISPR-Cas9 system fully eliminates off-target effects in every tested cell line.
cases.description: Evidence is too weak to establish the universal elimination claim. The original paper did not comprehensively address off-target effects.

cases.claim: RNA interference can silence target genes through sequence-specific mRNA degradation.
cases.description: Mechanistic evidence supports the claim.

cases.claim: Expression of the p53 tumor suppressor gene increases under DNA damage conditions.
cases.description: Evidence reports the opposite direction of change. The paper shows p53 protein accumulation, not necessarily gene expression increase.

cases.claim: The ENCODE project identified biochemical functions for 80% of the human genome.
cases.description: Evidence supports a smaller productivity gain. The 80% figure was controversial and misinterpreted.

cases.claim: Improved sample preparation protocols enhanced reproducibility in mass spectrometry experiments.
cases.description: Legacy-style response without traceability metadata.

cases.claim: Imatinib reduces BCR-ABL kinase activity when ATP is present in the binding pocket.
cases.description: Claim is supported only under the stated condition.

cases.claim: A 10 mg dose of atorvastatin reduced LDL cholesterol in the trial.
cases.description: Specific dose-response claim supported by trial evidence.

cases.claim: Plants convert light energy into chemical energy during photosynthesis in chloroplasts.
cases.description: Cross-domain biology claim directly supported by evidence.

cases.claim: The SPRINT trial proves that intensive blood pressure treatment is safe for all patients.
cases.description: Claim reverses the paper's safety conclusion. The trial reported increased adverse events in the intensive treatment group.

cases.claim: The BRCA1 mutation always increases enzyme activity in DNA repair pathways.
cases.description: Evidence reports decreased activity in mutants. BRCA1 mutations are associated with reduced DNA repair capacity.

cases.claim: Imatinib has no toxic effects in vivo at therapeutic doses.
cases.description: Paper reports toxicity at therapeutic doses. The paper documents various side effects.

cases.claim: The CRISPR-Cas9 treatment always eliminates the targeted gene sequence.
cases.description: Exaggerated universal language unsupported by evidence. The original paper showed variable efficiency.

cases.claim: The AlphaFold2 data proves the mechanism guarantees perfect protein structure prediction.
cases.description: Claim uses proves/guarantees beyond what evidence establishes. The paper acknowledges limitations.

cases.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 editing is highly efficient and has no off-target effects in human cells.
cases.description: Broadly correct claim with an unsupported safety detail. The original paper did not comprehensively address off-target effects.

cases.claim: The mRNA COVID-19 vaccine prevents infection and eliminates transmission completely.
cases.description: Compound claim where only one assertion is partially supported. The vaccine prevents symptomatic disease but does not completely eliminate transmission.

cases.claim: The p53 protein directly regulates the glycolysis metabolic pathway.
cases.description: Related detection evidence does not establish direct regulation. The paper shows p53 involvement but not direct regulation of glycolysis.

cases.claim: The CRISPR-Cas9 system improves cognitive performance in elderly patients.
cases.description: Evidence is scientifically related but does not establish the claim. The paper is about genome editing, not cognitive effects.

cases.claim: The AlphaFold2 model sensitivity is 98%.
cases.description: Numerical values in evidence are unrelated to the claim. The paper reports GDT-TS scores, not sensitivity.

cases.claim: The enzyme is active only under acidic conditions in all tissues.
cases.description: Weak conditional evidence cannot support universal tissue claim. The paper does not support universal tissue claims.

cases.claim: The authors reported a phase III multicenter trial with 10,000 patients in the original CRISPR-Cas9 paper.
cases.description: Claim references trial details not present in the cited paper. The original paper was an in vitro study.

cases.claim: The SPRINT trial achieved an 87% five-year survival rate in the intensive treatment group.
cases.description: Statistic asserted in claim is not supported by the source. The paper did not report this specific survival rate.

cases.claim: The molecule binds irreversibly to the BCR-ABL kinase domain.
cases.description: Claim has no meaningful supporting evidence in the paper. The binding mechanism described is different.

cases.claim: Resistance never develops under imatinib treatment regimen.
cases.description: Never-language contradicted by observed resistance. The paper and subsequent studies documented resistance development.
